plain.text: Sarai had not been able to have children. She had an Egyptian servant named Hagar. Sarai said to Abram, "The LORD has kept me from having children. Go and sleep with my servant; perhaps I can build a family through her." Abram agreed, and Hagar became pregnant. When Hagar knew she was pregnant, she began to despise Sarai. Sarai blamed Abram, who told her to do whatever she thought best. Sarai mistreated Hagar, and Hagar ran away. The angel of the LORD found her by a spring in the desert. "Hagar, servant of Sarai, where have you come from, and where are you going?" He told her to go back and promised that her descendants would be too many to count. She would have a son and name him Ishmael ("God hears"), for the LORD had heard her misery. Hagar gave a name to the LORD who spoke to her: "You are the God who sees me." She said, "Here I have seen the One who sees me!" Hagar bore Abram a son, and Abram named him Ishmael. Abram was eighty-six.

summary.bigIdea: When Sarai and Abram try to make God's promise happen their own way, it brings pain, but God sees and hears Hagar.
points: Sarai gives Hagar to Abram to have a child, and the plan causes conflict.
Hagar runs away, and the angel of the LORD finds her in the desert.
Hagar calls God "the God who sees me"; her son is named Ishmael, "God hears".
summary.reflection: Hagar discovered that God saw her when no one else did. Do you need to know that God sees you right now?
